records.text: On April 14, 2024, during Iran and Hezbollah's retaliation for Israel's bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus, the Egyptian aircraft SU-BTU flew from Cairo to Paris and stayed there for six days.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Similarly, on April 14th of 2024—I believe I wrote 25, but I think it's 24—there was Operation True Promise, okay? ... That's when Israel was being bombed by Iran and Hezbollah in retaliation because Israel had bombed the Iranian embassy in Damascus. ... Well, lo and behold, that same Egyptian plane took off, flew from Cairo, always to Paris, and it stayed there for six days.

verification.notes: No authoritative public historical flight record located establishes SU-BTU flying Cairo to Paris on April 14, 2024 or remaining there six days. Current flight-tracking pages do not expose sufficient historical detail. Audited public-record limitation; verification was attempted.

records.text: Hezbollah formed in the 1980s after Israel invaded southern Lebanon.
records.speaker: Ana Kasparian

appearances.snippet: You got to understand why Hezbollah exists in the first place. Hezbollah formed in the 1980s after Israel invaded southern Lebanon.

verification.notes: Authoritative historical summaries agree that Hezbollah emerged and was formed with Iranian backing after Israel 1982 invasion and occupation of southern Lebanon, with formal public organization following in the mid-1980s.

records.text: Candace Owens said the pagers used in the September 2024 attack were rigged with PETN and targeted Hezbollah operatives.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: OK, so you should know that the pagers were rigged, as I told you, with P-E-T-N explosive. The intended target were Hezbollah operatives.

verification.notes: Reuters reporting and later Mossad accounts confirm that the pagers were booby-trapped with PETN and supplied to Hezbollah personnel; civilians were also harmed.

sources.title: Israel Mossad spent years orchestrating Hezbollah pager plot - 60 Minutes
sources.relevance: Former Mossad agents describe weaponized pagers built and sold to Hezbollah through a supply-chain operation.

records.text: Candace Owens said Israel interrupted the pager supply chain by creating shell companies and selling rigged pagers to people affiliated with Hezbollah.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: How did they do it? Well, they interrupted the supply chain of pagers by creating a bunch of fake shell companies and selling the rigged pagers to people who were affiliated with Hezbollah.

verification.notes: Independent reporting and former Mossad agents confirm that Israeli intelligence used layered shell companies and a commercial supply-chain ruse to sell weaponized pagers to Hezbollah.

sources.title: Former Israeli spies describe exploding-device attack against Hezbollah
sources.relevance: Confirms the shell-company supply-chain ruse and sales to Hezbollah.

records.text: An unnamed Mossad agent said everything in Hezbollah's experience was controlled by Mossad behind the scenes and appeared normal.

appearances.snippet: Everything is controlled by us behind the scene. In their experience, everything is normal. Everything was 100% kosher, including businessmen, marketing, engineers, showroom, everything.

verification.notes: The 60 Minutes transcript directly records the former Mossad agent comparing the operation to The Truman Show and saying Hezbollah experienced a normal commercial environment controlled behind the scenes.
